summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727 KB bundle
details: The package's preinstall script (setup.mjs) is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0x identifiers with control-flow dispatch). On npm install it downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, unpacks it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a co-shipped 727 KB single-line bundle math_init.js. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (string-array-shuffle rotator over a several-thousand-entry constant table with a decoder function) and its bytes are opaque to static analysis. math_init.js is not listed in package.json's `files` array (which declares only bin/src/reference/CHANGELOG.md/NOTICE) yet ships in the tarball and is the exact file preinstall passes to Bun. The package is advertised as a pure-Node read-only documentation/CLI helper for the OneReach SDK — a role that has no need for an alternate language runtime or an opaque compiled bundle executing at install time. Executing the payload through Bun rather than Node bypasses standard Node-focused install-time inspection, and the obfuscation of both the preinstall wrapper and the executed bundle blocks review of what runs on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
